decisions.reason: It builds directly on the firm's wafer materials and process-integration know-how, so with its in-house R&D and project experience we would expect enough absorptive capacity to refine it rather than withdraw it.
This carrier wafer is very close to the firm's established thin-wafer handling and substrate business, making it easy to support commercially and technically within the existing knowledge base.

As a flagship product aligned with the firm's direction toward multifunctional packaging wafers, it is related enough to existing capabilities that management would likely continue learning and investing in it.
An off-the-shelf brand for standard glass and quartz wafers sits at the core of the firm's existing materials and customer base, so it has the lowest withdrawal risk.

Glass-based circuit boards are comparatively distant from the firm's narrow established substrate offer, so despite R&D strength the weaker knowledge overlap makes commercial improvement and scaling less likely.
